title: The Hero’s Secret Meeting
text: “…Will we be okay with the next wave?”
“Well… it’s not like we can’t do anything.”
And with that, Father smoothly brushes off Ren’s concerns.
“Anyway, we should keep costs to a minimum… no, we should treat the heroes fairly,”
Ren said, pointing at Trash.
“…Hmm. It seems the guild members let their personal feelings get in the way when dealing with the Shield Hero and the Spear Hero. I’ll apologize on behalf of the guild.”
He says this, but he absolutely refuses to bow his head. It’s crystal clear that deep down, this Trash can’t wait to see my Father suffer.
“The guild folks believed that farce and didn’t give Naofumi any work… huh?”
Ren muttered under his breath. Well, since it makes sense on some level, even though I can’t quite accept the situation, I’m nodding along for now.
“Then, as compensation, I’ll give you an additional 300 silver coins. Take them.”

Another money bag clattered onto the table. It’s striking how that Trash is furrowing his brow in disgust. The Crimson Swine’s forced smile gives him away instantly. It’s not Ren, but I’m getting sick of this farce—I’m doing my best just to keep from throwing up.
“…Well then, that concludes the distribution of aid funds for this round. Until the next wave, the heroes should each continue to train diligently. Dismissed!”

Oh? Isn’t he going to offer my Father a ‘severance payment’ or something? Hmm… I suppose he realizes that if he went that far, Ren would definitely call him out on it. If that happened, it would already be too late—he might even end up making Itsuki lose faith in the kingdom as well.
For now, it’s best to call it a day here. We left the castle right then and there.
“Hey… You’re in the way! Move it!”
“Sorry. That’s—”
It seems Ren was trying to come over to us but was blocked by his companions. Just then, Father quickly stepped in and approached them.
“What’s going on?”
“Ah, Naofumi. I was trying to talk to you guys, but these guys were getting in the way.”
Perhaps realizing it was already too late, Ren’s companions stepped back. Well… if we go by the previous loop, talking right here in the middle of town is dangerous.
“If we’re going to talk, I think a quieter place would be better. Of course, that doesn’t include your companions.”
“Ah… I see. Well then, let’s find a suitable spot. You guys wait at the tavern.”
“B-but… um…”
Ren’s companions looked frightened and tried to protest his order, but Ren just sighed in annoyance.

“What is it? You’re talking as if there’s something I’m not supposed to know. We heroes need to coordinate with each other. It’d be pointless if we ran into each other at the hunting grounds, wouldn’t it?”
Well, a mere adventurer can’t stop Ren.
“If you follow me any further, I’ll fire you all.”
“T-that’s a problem!”
Looking rather reluctant, Ren’s companions walked away. Ren sure does take some bold actions, doesn’t he?
“Then I’ll be your guide.”
“Can you handle it, Motoyasu-kun?”
“Leave it to me.”
So, I subtly approached Yuki-chan, Kou, and Sakura-chan and whispered in their ears.
“Let’s head toward the back alleys while keeping an eye out for anyone hiding nearby. If you spot anyone, please give me a signal.”
“Got it.”
“Hide-and-seek?”
“Are we looking for people who aren’t there?”

Filolial-sama has a keen ability to sense those in hiding, after all. Of course, there’s no guarantee that someone won’t slip past her detection, but this time I’ll be the one finding them, so it shouldn’t be a problem. Worst-case scenario, I’ll just have to eliminate them.
And so, with Ren in tow, we entered the back alley and moved forward. Well, is this about the right spot? I’ll cast a fire Magic spell in a low voice so no one else can hear.
“Liberation Fireflash.”

I cast a Magic spell that gently… reveals anyone hiding nearby. By the way, since it has offensive capabilities, if you’re hiding here carelessly, you’ll be consumed by the flames in an instant—it is, after all, “Liberation.”
“So, Ren, what brings you here?”

“Ah… After seeing everything that’s happened so far, I just can’t shake the feeling that something’s fishy about this country. I wanted to talk to Naofumi and the others, who are being blatantly discriminated against.”
“I see.”
My Father turned his gaze toward me. It seemed Ren’s suspicions had already turned into certainty. Sharing some information at this point was probably a necessary step.

“Actually, this country… seems to view the Shield Hero as a religious enemy. But if they openly discriminate against me, they’d face condemnation from neighboring countries and the rest of the world. So I think their goal is to secretly frame me for various crimes and assassinate me…”
“…I see. Indeed, looking back on everything that’s happened so far, it all adds up.”
Ren is nodding repeatedly. Indeed, given this situation and with all that evidence piled up, there’s no room for doubt.
“So the rape accusation was part of that scheme, too?”
“Yeah. I didn’t do it, and even though they’re slaves, I haven’t forced these girls to fight. They’re only slaves because it’s necessary.”
“That’s right! Big Bro hasn’t activated the slave mark even once!”
Keel answers as if it were his own business.
“I see. Then why don’t you leave this country?”
“Well, that’s…”

I think it’ll be hard for Ren to believe what I’m about to say. I’ve come from the future, and if I seek asylum in Siltvelt, Melromarc will start a war. It’s doubtful he’d believe that, on top of everything else, the Hero would get dragged into that war.
“We’ve got our own reasons, too. I want to change this country from the inside. That’s why I’m working as a traveling merchant, right?”
Nice comeback. It’s not a lie, mind you. Just as I’d expect from Father. Your quick-witted excuses are second to none.
“…You’ve chosen a rather troublesome method, haven’t you?”

Ren’s point is well taken. Come to think of it, it really is a troublesome approach. Considering how Trash and the Crimson Swine run amok, it’s harder to hold back my anger. Above all, Itsuki is incredibly annoying. Maybe I should smile as I recall that time he lost to my Father and ended up rolling around in a humiliating heap?
A burst of flames flared up behind us. It seems the assassins have arrived earlier than expected. But assassinating us is impossible.
“What’s that? It seems barbaric brawls are rampant in the back alleys.”
“I suppose so.”
Ren didn’t seem to have the slightest inkling that someone was secretly closing in on us.
“…I’ve no interest in getting dragged into some pointless power struggle. I’ll just do a bit of guild work, see how things go, and then make a run for Zeltoble.”
“Understood. Well then… I suppose so. I think this commotion will die down in a little while, so how about we meet up around then?”
“Not a bad idea, but do you know when exactly?”

Hmm… It’s dangerous to get too specific. Ren has a bit of a contrarian streak—I have a feeling that if I tell him not to go to Faubrey, he’ll go there anyway. For now, while we’re using Zeltoble as our base, it might be best to just leave him be.
“I suppose so… I think I’ll be able to use my teleportation skill soon, so wouldn’t it be best to meet up once a month?”
“...That’s certainly not a bad idea. Rumors about you guys might start circulating in Zeltoble, so we’ll just have to assess the situation as it goes.”
That’s about it, I suppose. There’s no point in talking to Ren as he is right now.
“But… how did you manage to beat Itsuki? Naofumi, have you been practicing a lot?”
“Speaking of which, Ren, there are all kinds of ways to enhance weapons. In fact, there are plenty of enhancement methods you don’t even know about. First of all—”
Father is teaching Ren how to enhance weapons. What a waste of time… Ren is currently convinced he’s in the world of the game he knows, so he’s just tuning it out.
“There’s no way the system is that complicated. Naofumi has just been practicing hard. You can’t actually do it, can you? Stop lying.”
While listening, Ren did make a few movements as if he were trying out the enhancement methods. But since it won’t work unless he truly believes it, there’s absolutely no way he could pull it off.

“Still, I can’t imagine Naofumi lying in a situation like this… No, even if he could, that’s probably just how Naofumi’s weapons work. Just as my world and Itsuki’s are different, the games we played were different, so maybe the weapons are different too.”
It seems Ren has already jumped to that conclusion. At this rate, there’s no hope for him to grow. That said… I wouldn’t really recommend getting into a long conversation here.
“Well, I can’t do it with my weapon, and Naofumi’s strength probably depends on his level. He must have worked hard alongside Motoyasu.”
“That’s true, but… hmm…”
Hesitating slightly, my Father wrapped up his conversation with Ren.
“Be careful at the border.”
“Don’t underestimate me. I can sense something like that.”

And with that, Ren slipped away. From what I heard while he was talking to my Father, it seems he’ll move on once he’s finished what he needs to do in this country to a certain extent. My Father, as the Shield Hero, probably can’t cross the border, but Ren… he should still be able to.

It’s a bit dangerous, but let’s assume he’s still perceived as someone who’s only within the bounds of what they suspect. If Ren’s life were to be targeted because of this, he’d surely come to my Father’s place. After all, even in his current state, Ren has surely gained enough strength that ordinary adventurers or the country’s soldiers wouldn’t stand a chance against him.

Once he takes the Ceremonial Magic class, that won’t be an issue anymore, but they’ll likely attack my Father first rather than trying to take out Ren. They’ll probably make it look like my Father kidnapped his Finacée, pit the two Heroes against each other, and then try to eliminate Ren. I think we have some breathing room until then.
